scope: Proposition A.5 (A pointwise joint density version) of the manuscript “Memory and precision in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Memory-and-precision-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a46ccc95821da009), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the same hypotheses as in Proposi- tion A.4. For the Gaussian density ϕδ, define wδ(r) = vmrm r δ2 ϕδ(re1), r > 0, (64) where e1 is a unit coordinate vector. This is a probability density on (0, ∞), and ϕδ is the corre- sponding mixture of uniform ball densities. Define F♯ (A, y) =    lim i→∞ F1/i(A, y), if this limit exists and is finite, 0, otherwise. (65) Then F♯ is jointly Borel. For every full-row-rank A, F♯(A, ·) is a density of A#µ up to a Lebesgue null set, and it is a density of ηµ with respect to λm. Moreover Z (F♯ )p dλm ≤ Bp . (66)
